dialect.detail: JMA ORCA medical receipt system (JMA standard receipt software), compiled with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL for Linux. Uses MCP (Message Control Program) linkage area pattern typical of ORCA subsystems.
evidence: PROCEDURE DIVISION USING MCPAREA SPAAREA LINKAREA SCRAREA
COPY Q01.INC / Q02.INC etc. screen copybooks
no EXEC CICS / no EXEC SQL

purpose.domain_detail: Japanese medical receipt (shinryo-hoshuu) system - patient inquiry/search screen (Q01: patient basic information lookup). Part of the JMA ORCA open-source medical billing system used by Japanese clinics.
purpose.summary: This program implements the patient inquiry screen (ORCGQ01) for the JMA ORCA medical receipt system. It handles patient search and display of basic patient information including patient number, name, sex, date of birth, address, insurance number, diagnosis (byomei), and medical treatment history. It is a screen-driven subprogram called via the ORCA MCP framework.

notable_features: MCP (Message Control Program) linkage pattern with MCPAREA/SPAAREA/LINKAREA/SCRAREA
Extensive use of COPY statements (36 copybooks) for screen layouts and data structures
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS - uses proprietary ORCA DB access layer (MCPDATA.INC)
Screen section via copybooks (Q01.INC through Q100.INC)
verdict.notes: Comments are encoded in Japanese EUC-JP but decoded as latin-1, producing mojibake in the displayed text. The program is clearly part of the well-known open-source JMA ORCA medical receipt system. File size (290KB, 7536 lines) and structure indicate a substantial production program. No COMP-3 usage is notable for a financial/medical system - likely uses BINARY or display numerics throughout.
